# Kpler & GrowthBook | Enterprise Setup (Technical clarification, commercial walkthrough)
Date: 2026-09-30 | Duration: 52m

## Summary
Kpler needs SSO and SCIM to automate user provisioning and avoid manually adding or removing users, but SSO is not included in its current Pro plan. Growth from 200 to more than 900 employees has increased this need. GrowthBook usage is steady, with feature flags widely used by engineers, while experimentation remains limited because the source-of-truth migration is delaying testing and the company prioritizes fast shipping. Warehouse-native metrics and automatic rollback were discussed but are not currently used. Kpler has about 91 seats, compared with the Pro plan’s 30-seat cap, and expects adoption to grow toward a realistic maximum of about 200 users. Enterprise provides unlimited seats, SSO, and CDN traffic, but the higher cost requires internal approval as the budget year closes. Pricing changes take effect at the end of October, with an annual agreement needed by then for the best terms. Rémi will investigate approval, while pricing details and a proposal will be emailed before a Tuesday follow-up.

## Keywords
growth book, SSO, SCIM, enterprise licensing, feature flags, pricing negotiation

## Action Items
**James Shannon**  
Provide pricing proposals with new seat limits (23:30)  
Engage Rémi Becheras for Enterprise justification (20:30)  

**Rémi Becheras**  
Follow up with internal stakeholders on proposal (32:00)  
Investigate budget approval for Enterprise agreement (34:32)  
Compare cost/benefit of Pro vs Enterprise plan (38:30)  

**Philippe Delorme**  
Send SSO and SCIM pricing questions (06:27)  
Investigate impact of reducing seats to 30 (36:58)  

**Marcel Geldner**  
Send contract and pricing details to Kpler (40:16)
